items.case: Petition by Arvind Kumar Singh (Samajwadi Party) against the Election Commission of India, filed 28 November 2025, Supreme Court
items.headline: Fresh challenges to electoral roll revision in Assam & UP; SC notice to EC on Assam plea
items.claim: A former MP of the Samajwadi Party petitioned the Supreme Court on 28 November 2025 against the revision in Uttar Pradesh and the notification behind it, ThePrint reported. The petition said the timeline was unreasonable, set unreasonable work expectations and came without practical training, and asked for a searchable database.
items.quote: This plea, filed by former MP and Samajwadi Party member Arvind Kumar Singh, says that the revision of the electoral roll in Uttar Pradesh was “totally flawed, biased and has prejudiced and hampered the well being of several individuals”.

items.headline: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 85,854 Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported, from more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 disclosures on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's website, that 87,127 deletion requests were filed by registration officers between 15 March and 2 April 2026 and that 85,854 of them gave no reason. Four registration officers told it that ERONET generated a Form 7 carrying their digital signature whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing. It also reported that 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals were accepted after the deadline.
items.quote: Our analysis of the data scraped from the ECI’s website shows that 85,854 (98.5 percent) of the 87,127 requests filed by EROs and AEROs have no reason mentioned for deletion.
items.response: The Collective said the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission had not replied by publication. On 13 October 2026 IANS, in The Hans India, reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office calling the claims misleading and saying "Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure."

bulk.filer: Registration officers and assistant registration officers. Officers said ERONET generated a Form 7 in their name whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing.
bulk.outcome: None of the 87,127 gives a reason for the deletion.

items.headline: In UP SIR, ECI Software Auto-generated 87,127* Forms to Delete Voters Without a Reason
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that in the Tarabganj and Pilibhit Assembly constituencies 90 per cent of Form 7 deletion requests were against Muslim voters, and that in Tarabganj 188 objections were filed under one name on the same date against voters of one booth. It said the published data give no identity of an objector beyond a name, so the objectors cannot be checked.
items.quote: Out of 4.3 lakh Form 7 applications, in two assembly constituencies in UP, people with the same name filed hundreds of requests almost exclusively against Muslim voters. In Tarabganj and Pilibhit assembly constituencies, 90 percent of the deletion requests filed were against Muslims.
items.response: The Collective said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission and had no reply by publication. The report does not say how it determined the voters' religion.

bulk.filer: One name, on one date, against voters of one booth. The published data give no other detail of the objector.

items.headline: UP Chief Electoral Officer rejects media report alleging 'mysterious' 16.18 lakh voter additions
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that 16.18 lakh Form 6 applications were collected in Uttar Pradesh before the draft roll of 6 January 2026 and that their details were not published. The Chief Electoral Officer rejected the report on X, The New Indian Express reported, saying the forms were collected by booth officers during enumeration under the Commission's instructions.
items.quote: The clarification came in response to a report titled “The Mysterious 16.18 Lakh Voters Added to Uttar Pradesh’s Roll”, which questioned the collection and subsequent processing of 16.18 lakh Form-6 applications during the SIR.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer said "The allegations levelled in the report are not correct as these are based on faulty assumptions and are therefore categorically denied", that only Form 6s received after the draft had to go in the published list of claims, and that "There is no formula or logic for the acceptance of forms to adhere to a particular percentage."

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: Residents of a village in Siddharthnagar went to the Mishrauliya police station to complain that about 86 villagers were being objected to by Form 7, BBC News Hindi reported. The booth officer told local media that one person had handed him all 86 forms, that every voter named in them was Muslim and that all of them were present.
items.quote: सभी 86 फ़ॉर्मों में जिनके नाम काटने के लिए आवेदन किया गया है वे सभी मुसलमान हैं. सभी मौजूद भी हैं. इसलिए जैसा जो भी है, मैं अपनी रिपोर्ट लगा दूंगा.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer told BBC News Hindi "जिन लोगों के नाम कटवाने के लिए फ़ॉर्म 7 मिला है, उन्हें नोटिस दिए बिना और सुनवाई के बगैर नाम नहीं काटे जाएंगे."

bulk.filer: One person, the booth officer said.
bulk.outcome: Residents complained at the Mishrauliya police station. The booth officer said every voter named was present.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: A Samajwadi Party former minister from Gonda showed BBC News Hindi printed Form 7s from the Karnalganj constituency that carried the district, polling station and constituency already filled in but no objector's name, and said more than 6,000 deletions were being sought there. BBC News Hindi reported that every form had 'already enrolled' ticked as the reason.
items.quote: इसके अलावा जिस कॉलम पर आपत्ति का कारण दर्ज करना होता है, सभी फ़ॉर्मों में उनमें 'पहले से नामांकित' पर टिक किया गया है.
items.response: At a press conference on 6 February the Chief Electoral Officer said "कोई भी राजनीतिक दल का कार्यकर्ता एक दिन में 10 फ़ॉर्म से ज़्यादा नहीं जमा कर सकता है. जो फ़ॉर्म 7 जमा किए गए हैं, उनकी जांच होगी. अभी कोई नाम नहीं काटे जा रहे हैं." The BJP called the Samajwadi Party's allegations baseless.

bulk.filer: The report does not say who filed them. The Samajwadi Party gave the figure.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party MP for Badaun gave the District Magistrate a list alleging that objections were being filed to a plan, BBC News Hindi reported, including a Form 7 against an elected ward member of Kakrala who said he had been a voter since 2012. In Datganj, a BJP Assembly convener whose name was on an objection told BBC News Hindi he had signed forms the party gave him and did not personally know the voter.
items.quote: मैं बीजेपी का विधानसभा संयोजक हूं. मुझे पार्टी की तरफ़ से कुछ फ़ॉर्म मिले थे, हमने इसे साइन कर दिया
items.response: The BJP called the allegations baseless, BBC News Hindi reported, and the Commission said complaints would be examined.

bulk.filer: A BJP Assembly convener said he signed forms the party gave him.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: The Congress said its workers in Sant Kabir Nagar caught Form 7s being submitted to delete villagers and that the man whose signature was on them denied signing, BBC News Hindi reported. BBC News Hindi said it could not verify the video of the incident.
items.quote: इसमें जिस व्यक्ति के हस्ताक्षर थे, वह इनकार कर रहा है कि ये हस्ताक्षर उसके हैं.
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer said "इस पर उस व्यक्ति को एफ़आईआर दर्ज करानी चाहिए जिनका हस्ताक्षर फर्ज़ी है." He said officers had been told to make sure each Form 7 was submitted by the person whose signature it carried.

bulk.filer: The man whose signature was on them denied signing, the Congress said.

items.headline: एसआईआर: यूपी में मतदाता सूची से नाम कटवाने वाले फ़ॉर्म 7 पर क्या है विवाद
items.claim: A BJP minister in the Uttar Pradesh government alleged that 9,200 bogus voters were enrolled in Varanasi South and asked for them to be checked again, BBC News Hindi reported.
items.quote: वाराणसी से यूपी सरकार में मंत्री रवींद्र जायसवाल ने आरोप लगाया है कि वाराणसी दक्षिण में 9200 फर्ज़ी मतदाता दर्ज हैं
items.response: The Varanasi District Magistrate told the media "इस मामले में बीजेपी की तरफ से शिकायत मिली है.अलग-अलग बूथों की शिकायत है. जांच के बाद उचित कार्रवाई की जाएगी."

items.headline: सपा ने फॉर्म-7 में धांधली का आरोप लगाया:सुल्तानपुर में मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाने के खिलाफ प्रदर्शन
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party demonstrated at the Sultanpur Collectorate on 3 February 2026 and gave the District Magistrate a memorandum for the Chief Election Commissioner, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The party alleged that pre-printed Form 7s in one handwriting were being submitted in bulk against voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities, and asked for them to be cancelled and for FIRs under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
items.quote: पार्टी के अनुसार, गाँवों और नगरों में 'प्री-प्रिंटेड' फॉर्म-7 थोक में जमा किए जा रहे हैं। इन फॉर्मों में एक ही लिखावट और छपे-छपाए विवरण पाए गए हैं, जो बूथ लेवल ऑफिसर (बीएलओ) के पास बड़ी संख्या में पहुँच रहे हैं।

bulk.outcome: The Samajwadi Party demonstrated at the Sultanpur Collectorate and asked for the forms to be cancelled.

items.headline: सोनभद्र में मतदाता सूची से नाम हटाने की साजिश:फॉर्म 7 में झूठी आपत्तियां दर्ज कर कटवाए जा रहे नाम, जांच शुरू
items.claim: Form 7 objections were filed against 14 voters of one community in part 14 of the Sadar constituency in Sonbhadra, Dainik Bhaskar reported. The booth officer inspected on the spot and found the objections false. Two of the 14 had died and the rest were present. A Samajwadi Party district office-holder raised the case with the District Magistrate.
items.quote: स्थलीय निरीक्षण में इनमें से दो की मृत्यु की पुष्टि हुई, जबकि अन्य सभी मौके पर उपस्थित पाए गए।

bulk.filer: One person, the booth officer told a Samajwadi Party office-holder.
bulk.outcome: The booth officer inspected on the spot and found the objections false.

items.headline: Akhilesh Yadav flags "massive conspiracy" in SIR, questions use of pre-printed form 7 in UP villages
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party president alleged on X that pre-printed Form 7s were being distributed in villages to strike off opposition voters, that the objectors listed on them could not be traced and that signatures were forged, The Economic Times reported from ANI. He said voters from backward, Dalit and minority communities were most affected.
items.quote: Under SIR, who is distributing the pre-printed Form 7 in villages (through which someone can conspire to get another's name struck off by raising an objection)?

items.headline: "Fraud across the 403 seats": Akhilesh Yadav threatens to release proof of SIR fraud
items.claim: The Samajwadi Party president said on 12 October 2026 that the final roll in Uttar Pradesh holds lakhs of fake entries, with one person registered as many as ten times, and that the party would release lists for several constituencies, ANI reported.
items.quote: There are lakhs of fake votes in Uttar Pradesh. A single person has as many as ten votes registered. We have identified such fake votes in several assembly constituencies... we will release the list.

items.headline: Ctrl+Alive+Delete: 3 living voters in Lucknow marked 'dead' in SIR draft roll, struck off list
items.claim: Three living residents of one address in the Lucknow North constituency were listed as dead in the draft roll of 6 January 2026, The Times of India reported. All three had voted on 27 October 2025 and held acknowledgements for the enumeration forms they handed to the booth officer. At their booth 41 of 1,241 voters were marked dead.
items.quote: At this particular booth, the Booth Level Officer (BLO) declared 41 out of 1,241 voters as dead.
items.response: The Times of India reported that the Chief Electoral Officer advised everyone missing from the draft to apply on Form 6 as new voters.

items.headline: ‘BLOs facing harassment in Gautam Buddha Nagar amid SIR Phase-2’: UP teachers’ body submits memorandum to DM
items.claim: The Gautam Buddh Nagar unit of the Uttar Pradesh Primary Teachers' Association wrote to the District Magistrate on 24 November 2025 alleging mental harassment of the about 1,800 teachers deployed as booth officers, two days after FIRs were registered against more than 60 booth officers and seven supervisors under section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, The Indian Express reported. The association asked for the FIRs to be withdrawn and said the Commission's app did not work in rural areas.
items.quote: However, you or officials under your direction have been registering FIRs and adverse entries which is leading to the mental harassment of the teachers
items.response: The Indian Express reported that the FIRs were lodged on the orders of the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Medha Rupam, against booth officers alleged to have shown a lack of compliance.

items.headline: ‘Denied medical leave’, booked for ‘not signing attendance’: BLOs say UP SIR is inhumane
items.claim: Newslaundry reported that Ghaziabad registered an FIR against 21 employees for negligence in booth officer duties on 27 November 2025, after Gautam Buddh Nagar's FIRs, and that glitches in the Commission's mobile application were a main reason for slow digitisation. The Ghaziabad complainant, a deputy tehsildar, admitted the app sometimes hung. The teachers' association letter cited app glitches and repeated OTP failures.
items.quote: A key reason for lagging in the digitisation effort has been the technical glitches in the EC’s national mobile application.
items.response: Officials told Newslaundry the FIRs were for negligence. An electoral registration officer said "Those who do not work will face action." Newslaundry said it sent questions to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's office.

items.headline: Four BLOs die amid mounting pressure during electoral revision drive in UP
items.claim: After a lekhpal supervising the revision died by suicide in Bindki, Fatehpur, the Lekhpal Association protested, would not let the body be taken for post-mortem until a case was registered, and announced a boycott of SIR work unless action was taken, The New Indian Express reported.
items.quote: It also announced a boycott of SIR work from Thursday unless action was taken against those responsible for the death.

items.headline: Four BLOs die amid mounting pressure during electoral revision drive in UP
items.claim: The New Indian Express reported four deaths of officers on revision duty in Uttar Pradesh that families tied to workload. They were a lekhpal supervisor in Fatehpur who died by suicide a day before his wedding, after what his family said were threats of dismissal, a teacher who collapsed on duty in Bareilly, a teacher in Gonda who died by suicide and an officer in Lucknow who had a brain haemorrhage. In Fatehpur police registered an FIR for abetment against a revenue officer and unnamed officials.
items.quote: Police have filed an FIR against senior officials on abetment charges.
items.response: The paper reported that the family had first named the electoral registration officer and was made to change the complaint, which the Additional Superintendent of Police, Fatehpur, denied.

items.headline: Another BLO dies by suicide, blamed SIR work pressure in heartbreaking video
items.claim: A 46-year-old assistant teacher on booth officer duty since 7 October died by suicide at home in Moradabad, police said, leaving a note to the district Basic Education Officer saying he could not meet the SIR targets, India Today reported.
items.quote: I have been working day and night but am unable to meet the SIR targets. My nights have become unbearable due to anxiety.
items.response: The District Magistrate said "Preliminary information suggests he died by suicide. His quality of work was excellent. Anganwadi employees were deployed to assist him. Both administrative and police probes are underway." The Commission extended the SIR schedule by a week the same day.

items.headline: Hathras UP BLO dies amid SIR poll row; government agrees to debate next week
items.claim: A 40-year-old assistant teacher working as a booth officer in Hathras collapsed at home and died on the way to hospital, The Telegraph reported. His family said he had been under stress since starting the work. The paper counted three booth officer deaths in Uttar Pradesh since the previous Sunday.
items.quote: A booth-level officer (BLO) in Uttar Pradesh’s Hathras district died on the way to a hospital from his home in Sikandra Rao town on Tuesday morning.
items.response: The District Magistrate called the death unfortunate, said the cause would be clear after the post-mortem, and said the administration would explore a job for the officer's wife.

items.headline: Congress alleges voter roll manipulation in UP's Pilibhit, seeks probe into SIR process
items.claim: The Uttar Pradesh Congress alleged at a press conference in Lucknow that in Pilibhit Sadar the names of 13,150 voters were changed between July and September, after the final roll of 10 April 2026, while their EPIC and serial numbers stayed the same, PTI reported. The party said 884 names of people still living there were deleted and 2,600 names of people who did not live there were added, and that the changes appeared to have been made in batches. It asked for an inquiry and said it would go to court. These are the Congress's allegations.
items.quote: If the same EPIC number is assigned to another person, the original voter may face an identity mismatch at the time of voting and be denied the right to vote,
items.response: The report carries no response. The next day The Wire reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, after an inquiry found that searching some EPIC numbers online showed other voters' details, had ordered the constituency's Electoral Registration Officer and Voter Registration Centre operator off roll duties and legal action against them.
items.note: PTI in The Hindu, published 21 October 2026, 7:11 pm IST, read in full on 22 October 2026 via Firecrawl. The quote is Supriya Shrinate's. The report calls the roll of 10 April the 'final draft'; the site holds Uttar Pradesh's final roll as published on 10 April 2026. The example voters the party named are private persons and are not named here. Speakers: Rajendra Pal Gautam, Aradhana Mishra, Supriya Shrinate, Imran Masood.

items.headline: Pilibhit Voter Roll Irregularities: FIR Against Two SDMs, Computer Operator Over 10,470 Entries
items.claim: An FIR was lodged on 22 October against the two Sub-Divisional Magistrates who had served as Pilibhit's Electoral Registration Officers and a computer operator at the constituency's Voter Registration Centre, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, The Wire reported. The Chief Electoral Officer's inquiry found that the operator had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications to change voters' details between 31 May and 29 August 2026, of which 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected, and that the office held no forms or records for any of them. The two officers were moved to district headquarters and the operator's services were ended. The District Election Officer was told to examine every Form 6 and Form 7 entry made by the same operator from 10 April to 21 October.
items.quote: No forms or records related to any of these entries were found available in the office,
items.response: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. Officials said the entries found irregular were being corrected, and the District Magistrate said the rolls of every constituency in the district would be cleaned up in a day or two.
items.note: By Omar Rashid, posted 22 October 2026, 11:45 pm IST, read in full on 23 October 2026 from The Wire's content API with curl. The FIR itself was not available to the reporter. The quote is the CEO's, Navdeep Rinwa. The report names the officers and the operator, and the site does not. The parties' claims about which voters were affected are theirs and are not carried. The Wire's report of 22 October, 2:38 pm, on the CEO's first order was also read.

items.headline: Six election officials removed in U.P. after SP flags voter list errors
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, took five booth level officers and a computer assistant off all roll work on 24 October and began ending their services, after an inquiry into the roll of the Azamgarh Assembly constituency (347), The Hindu reported. The Samajwadi Party had said at a press conference that one elector's name appeared ten times on that roll. The District Election Officer's report found the name 13 times in Hindi. Two of the entries had been taken up for deletion, and the other 11 belonged to 11 different people living in Azamgarh, ten of whose names and details were being corrected through Form 8. The Chief Electoral Officer ordered charge sheets and departmental proceedings against the Electoral Registration Officer of the time and two Assistant Electoral Registration Officers, with action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, and asked for a report on the rolls of every constituency in the district within a week.
items.quote: In response to the clerical lapses, the CEO directed the immediate removal of the responsible computer assistant and five BLOs from voter registration work.
items.response: The finding is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. His office said a further entry with the same name, in the Chauri Chaura constituency of Gorakhpur district, belonged to a different elector. The Indian Express quoted him saying the three officers would face action for negligence and laxity in supervision while the roll was prepared.
items.note: By Mayank Kumar in The Hindu, published 25 October 2026, 1:01 am IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 25 October 2026. The Indian Express report by Bhupendra Pandey (25 October 2026, 8:07 am IST) and The Wire's by Omar Rashid (24 October 2026, 10:36 pm IST, read through its content API) were read as well and agree on the figures. The Hindu says deletion proceedings had begun for the two entries, and The Indian Express and The Wire say they had already been deleted under the rules. The Hindu and The Indian Express date the Samajwadi Party's press conference 15 October and The Wire dates it 16 October. The Wire reports that the elector had filed a Form 6 around May, after the draft roll of 6 January. All three reports name the elector, and the site does not. The headline is The Hindu's own.

items.headline: SIR exercise: After Pilibhit, Azamgarh roll ‘errors’, UP CEO orders scrutiny of all Forms 6, 7, 8 filled by computer assistants
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, ordered on 25 October that every Form 6, Form 7 and Form 8 entered by computer assistants between the final roll of 10 April and 24 October be checked again, after the errors found in the rolls of Pilibhit and Azamgarh, The Indian Express reported. Computer assistants may no longer enter forms received on paper, which booth level officers are to digitise through the BLO App. Electoral Registration Officers are to review pending forms every day, and officials were told not to share their ERONET login IDs and passwords, were directed to study Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, which deals with breaches of official duty in preparing the roll, and were warned of strict action. The office pulled up the District Election Officers of Bulandshahr, Sitapur, Ghaziabad and Aligarh for late reports on complaints of duplicate voters circulated on social media, and directed that the draft rolls of the coming Special Summary Revision carry no duplicate entries.
items.quote: “All such forms must be digitised by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) through the BLO App,” the directive stated.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. They followed a virtual meeting with Divisional Commissioners, District Election Officers, registration officers and computer assistants, held to prepare for the Special Summary Revision, which The Hindu dates 24 October. The Hindu reports the same directions from an official statement, says officials were warned of action under Section 32, and adds that the section provides for imprisonment of at least three months and up to two years, with a fine.
items.note: By Maulshree Seth in The Indian Express, published 26 October 2026, 9:21 am IST (updated 10:36 am), read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 26 October 2026. The report says the Chief Electoral Officer gave the directions on Sunday, 25 October. The Hindu's report by Mayank Kumar and Sreeparna Chakrabarty (26 October 2026, 12:25 am IST) was read in full the same way and agrees on the period from 10 April, the bar on computer assistants entering paper forms, Section 32 and the four districts. The Indian Express report names the elector whose name appeared 13 times in Azamgarh, who is a private person and is not named here. It follows up-21 to up-23.

items.headline: FIR in UP Eight Months After Man Who Cannot Sign Says Forged Signature Was Used to Delete 26 Voters
items.claim: A first information report was registered on 24 October against unknown persons, under sections 318(4), 336(3) and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for cheating and forgery, over Form 7 applications that sought the deletion of 26 electors at booth 96 in the Sultanpur Sadar constituency, The Wire reported. The forms were presented as signed by an elector who has said publicly that he cannot read or write and uses his thumbprint. The complaint was made by the lekhpal who supervises the booth, and it does not say who submitted the forms. The Samajwadi Party raised the case in February (up-10), and its president Akhilesh Yadav presented the elector to the media in Lucknow on 8 February.
items.quote: Nevertheless, the BLO’s acceptance of incomplete Form-7 applications without verification was deemed an act of negligence in election-related duties, Rinwa noted.
items.response: Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said on 26 October that the report of the District Election Officer of Sultanpur found the forms had been given to the booth level officer, and that no action was taken on them because they did not carry the applicant's full name, EPIC number or mobile number. He said the booth level officer had been relieved of all election work and that disciplinary action had been recommended.
items.note: The Wire, by Omar Rashid, published 27 October 2026, 12:30 pm IST, read in full through The Wire's API with curl on 27 October 2026. The Wire says it reviewed a copy of the complaint. The report says the matter first came to light on 1 February and that booth 96 is at the primary school in Arjunpur in Jaisinghpur tehsil. The lekhpal is a government official and is named in the report. The elector is a private person and is not named here. The report also says Akhilesh Yadav gave the elector Rs 1 lakh. It does not say how many of the 26 electors were deleted, and the Chief Electoral Officer's account is that no action was taken on the forms.

bulk.filer: In the name of an elector who has said he cannot read or write.

items.case: The petitioners' interim application on Form 7 in the SIR matters concerning Uttar Pradesh, Kerala and Chhattisgarh, Supreme Court
items.headline: UP SIR: Supreme Court asks ECI to take steps against filing Form 7 applications in bulk for voter deletion
items.claim: The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana directed on 30 October that the petitioners give the Election Commission's senior counsel a note of the irregularities in Form 7 applications in Uttar Pradesh that they say remain unresolved, and that the Commission then examine the facts, take corrective steps and file a compliance report, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioners said the Court had asked the Commission on 5 August to respond to their interim application on Form 7 applications submitted before booth level officers in Chhattisgarh, Kerala and Uttar Pradesh, and that the issues in the first two states had since been addressed. He said 32 forms had been filed in one constituency against members of one community, that two forms on record were signed by the booth level officer, and that the Commission's affidavit carried material inconsistencies. He said FIRs had been directed in Telangana and Karnataka over similar filings and that nothing was done in Uttar Pradesh. Senior Advocate D.S. Naidu, for the Commission, said bulk Form 7 applications had been submitted and that officers checked them, found them false and did not act on them.
items.quote: The irregularities which have been brought to the notice of the Court shall be submitted to learned senior counsel appearing for the Election Commission of India by way of a note. On receipt thereof, let the Election Commission examine the factual aspects, thereafter take necessary corrective steps and file a compliance report,
items.response: Naidu said the Commission can examine further claims once a formal complaint is filed. LawChakra notes that the Court made no finding on the petitioners' allegations.
items.note: By Debayan Roy in Bar and Bench, published 30 October 2026 at 7:08 am UTC (12:38 pm IST), read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 30 October 2026. items.headline: DMs to be held accountable for voter list glitches, says UP chief electoral officer
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, said on 30 October that each District Election Officer would be held accountable for unnecessary pending cases, inactive users, incomplete profiles, errors in the roll or lax supervision in the district, Hindustan Times reported. District Election Officers are to log in to ECINET every day, review the receipt and disposal of Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 daily, and see that no form stays pending at any level. No officer is to share a user ID, password or OTP. A call request made through the Book a Call with BLO facility is not to stay pending for more than 48 hours, and a booth level officer who marks a request Contacted or Unavailable without contacting the elector is to face strict action. Rinwa also sought an explanation from the present District Election Officer of Pilibhit and his predecessor over the roll of Pilibhit Sadar, where an inquiry found that 13,779 wrong forms had been entered between 31 May and 29 August 2026 and 10,470 of them accepted.
items.quote: If any district finds unnecessarily pending cases, inactive users, incomplete profiles, inaccurate voter lists, or lax supervision, the DEO will be held accountable, and appropriate action will be considered based on the merits of the case,
items.response: The directions and the request for an explanation are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report gives no reply from the two District Election Officers.
items.note: By Rajesh Kumar Singh in Hindustan Times, Lucknow, published 31 October 2026 at 7:56 am IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 31 October 2026. The quote is Rinwa's words as the paper prints them. The Hindu (Mayank Kumar, published 31 October 2026 at 12:45 am IST, read in full the same way) prints the official statement of 30 October with the same directions and cites Section 13CC of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 for the District Election Officer's responsibility. It does not carry the Pilibhit figures. The 10,470 forms are the figure of the inquiry behind the FIR of up-22. The report names the two District Magistrates, who are officials.

items.headline: ECI’s Software and Rules Allow the Pilibhit Fake-Voter Playbook to Run Anywhere in India
items.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported that it compared the Commission's data for 55 of Pilibhit's 419 booths with the final roll of 10 April 2026, matching entries by EPIC number, and found 2,691 entries in which the elector's name and the relative's name had been replaced by different names, 5.7 per cent of the electors at those booths. It said 2,372 of the changes were made in August, 656 of them on 19 August within 7.4 minutes between 6.26 pm and 6.34 pm, and that 523 were made on 31 August within 19.4 minutes. It said the Urdu roll still carried the original details where the English and Hindi rolls had been changed. It checked 15 of the cases on the ground against two government photo identity documents for each and found that the documents matched the original entries in the final roll. When it checked again eight days after the Chief Electoral Officer's finding of 22 October, 2,638 of the 2,691 changed entries were still on the roll. Two booth level officers told it that the tehsil office asked them to verify a set of Form 8 applications and then told them, before they began, that the applications had already been resolved.
items.quote: Before his admission, we had independently verified the injection of 2,691 fake voters in just 55 booths of Pilibhit. Eight days after the Uttar Pradesh (UP) CEO acknowledged the fraud, we rechecked and found that 2,638 of these fake voters were still on the Pilibhit voter roll.
items.response: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and to the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer and that neither had replied by publication. The Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 22 October, which the report links, said the computer assistant at the constituency's voter registration centre had entered 13,779 Form 8 applications between 31 May and 29 August 2026, 4,717 of them up to 16 July and 9,062 from 17 July, that no form or record of any of them was found in the office, and that 10,470 were approved and 3,309 rejected. It ordered legal action against the operator and the two registration officers who served in those periods, departmental proceedings against both officers and the end of the operator's services, and said the wrong entries were being corrected under the rules. The report says a computer operator and two registration officers were suspended, which the press note does not say.
items.note: By Ayushi Kar, Shubhangi Derhgawen, Sumedha Mittal and Dikshya Koirala, edited by Nitin Sethi, in The Reporters' Collective. The page gives 31 October 2026 as the date of publication and of the last update, and its structured data gives 30 October 2026. Read in full from the page with curl on 31 October 2026, with its two figures (a screenshot of text searches of the ECINET Android app's code and an animated table of Pilibhit entries) opened and read. The figures are quoted in the report as follows. 'We then worked with technology and data analysts to download and analyse two sets of voter data for 55 of Pilibhit’s 419 booths.' 'Across just 55 booths, they found that 2,691 genuine voters had been surreptitiously deleted. That is 5.7 percent of the total voting population at these booths.' 'Most of the fake voters (2,372) were inserted into the voter roll in the month of August.' 'Of these, 656 fake voters were inserted on a single day, August 19. On the server, all these names were modified after office hours, within 7.4 minutes between 6.26 pm and 6.34 pm.' 'On that day, 523 names were modified between 3.43 pm and 4.02 pm, within 19.4 minutes.' 'In the Urdu database, the legitimate voters’ details had not been changed, while in the other two languages they had been replaced with the fake voters’ details.' 'In addition, we verified 15 such cases of deletions and insertion of fake voters on the ground.' 'We independently examined data from 55 polling booths in Pilibhit and verified 2,691 manipulated entries, all involved Muslim voters.' The entries were changed on Form 8 under the same EPIC numbers, so the report's 'deleted' is its word and the site's measure of names deleted does not count them. The report gives the day of the recheck only as eight days after the acknowledgement, and the press note it links (x.com/ceoup/status/2113259159127036128) is dated 22 October 2026. That press note, read in full from the post through api.fxtwitter.com, orders legal action under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against the operator and the registration officers posted up to 16 July and from 17 July to 29 August, departmental proceedings against both registration officers and the end of the operator's services, and asks for a report on the assistant registration officers. It gives the entry of the 13,779 forms as between 31 May and 29 August, while the report gives 31 August as a day on which 523 names were modified on the server. The report does not say whether its times are of entry or approval. The report says the operator and two EROs were suspended. The report names electors and shows their names and part of their EPIC numbers in its table. They are private persons and are not named here. The booth level officers are given by role. It follows up-21, up-22, up-24 and up-27. The weakness in the rules and software that the same report describes is soft-44. Second reading: the first reading's claim ended with the report's statement that the entries 'all involved Muslim voters'. It is left out of the claim. The report states it in one sentence, does not return to it, does not put it in its summary and does not say how it established it, and the site states nothing on religion in its own voice.

items.headline: Computer assistants in U.P. ERO offices to lose ECINET login IDs after Pilibhit misuse claims
items.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, directed on 31 October that the login IDs of all computer assistants working on the ECINET portal in the offices of Electoral Registration Officers across the state be deactivated at once, after complaints and information from Pilibhit district about the misuse of those IDs, The Hindu reported from an official statement. The computer assistants work as operators of the voter registration centres. The report puts their number at about 806, two in each Assembly constituency. Registration officers were asked to report compliance at the earliest, and the firm concerned was directed to end at once the services of the outsourced computer assistant involved in the case of the Pilibhit constituency (127).
items.quote: “The concerned firm has been directed to immediately terminate the service of the involved outsourced computer assistant in the case of Assembly Constituency 127-Pilibhit,” the statement said.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. His office's press note of 31 October, posted on X, addresses them to the District Election Officers. They are to have the login ID of every voter registration centre operator in every constituency disabled, so that no operator can do any work on the ECINET portal through it, obtain confirmation from each registration officer, check the action themselves and send a compliance report at once. The report gives no response from the firm or from the operator.
items.note: By Sreeparna Chakrabarty in The Hindu, New Delhi, published 31 October 2026 at 7:41 pm IST (updated 7:43 pm IST), read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 1 November 2026. The page marks the article as not free to read, and its JSON-LD carried the whole text. The quote is the official statement as the report prints it. The press note of the Chief Electoral Officer's office, dated Lucknow, 31 October 2026, was read in full in Hindi from the post x.com/ceoup/status/2116463790569189657 (posted 3:04 pm IST) through api.fxtwitter.com on 1 November 2026. Its three headings, in English translation, read 'Directions to District Election Officers to deactivate with immediate effect the login IDs of computer assistants (voter registration centre operators) of ERO offices on the ECINET portal', 'EROs will confirm the deactivation of the computer assistants' login IDs' and 'Directions given for the immediate termination of the service of the computer assistant involved in the case of Assembly Constituency 127-Pilibhit'. The press note does not give the number of operators and does not name the Chief Electoral Officer. The report states that KND Engineers and Consultants (India) Private Limited, registered in Gorakhpur, is the company to which the hiring of operators is now outsourced, in a sentence whose remainder it attributes to sources who spoke to The Hindu. Those sources said the companies change each year after a tender while the employees are drawn from the same list on a government portal, most of them having worked as operators for eight to ten years, and that the computer assistants were given access to the portal because many booth level officers were at first not adequately trained on the BLO app. The report also recalls the allegation of opposition parties, the Congress among them, about Pilibhit Sadar (up-21), the 13 entries under one name in Azamgarh (up-23) and the order of 25 October (up-24). The elector named in the Azamgarh entries is a private person and is not named here. Neither the report nor the press note names the operator. It follows up-21 to up-28.

items.headline: EC Orders Suspension of Two Election Officers in UP Following Pilibhit Revelations
items.claim: The Election Commission directed in a letter of 31 October to the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh that two Electoral Registration Officers of the Pilibhit constituency, Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary, be placed under suspension at once, The Wire reported. Their chargesheets are to be sent to the Commission for vetting, and they cannot be reinstated without its prior approval. The Commission directed that Section 198 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which the report describes as a public servant disobeying the law with intent to cause injury, be added to the existing FIR against the two officers and a voter registration centre computer operator, and that the cases be pursued in court. It asked for the Pilibhit District Election Officer's report on the rolls of all four constituencies in the district within a week, and for a report within three days on the action taken against the computer operator and five Assistant Electoral Registration Officers of the Pilibhit seat. The FIR of 22 October followed an inquiry that found 13,779 Form 8 applications entered between 31 May and 29 August, 10,470 of them approved, with no application forms or documents for them in the office.
items.quote: The EC on Saturday (October 31) directed in a letter to the chief electoral officer (CEO) of Uttar Pradesh that EROs Mayank Goswami and Hemant Chaudhary be placed under immediate suspension.
items.response: The directions are the Commission's own. The report gives no reply from the two officers. PTI, in a report carried by ThePrint, gives the same suspension, the vetting of the chargesheets, the bar on reinstatement and the addition of Section 198.
items.note: The Wire Staff, published 1 November 2026 at 11:14 pm IST (post_date_gmt 17:44:40), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) on 2 November 2026. PTI in ThePrint (published 1 November 2026 at 1:45 pm IST, auto-generated from the PTI feed) was read in full with curl the same day. The report on all four constituencies and the five Assistant Electoral Registration Officers are in The Wire only. The two Electoral Registration Officers are officials and are named. Both reports name the computer operator, who is not named here. The Commission's letter itself was not found. It follows up-22, up-27 and up-29.

items.headline: Uttar Pradesh chief electoral officer directs DEOs to re-examine all rejected Form 6 applications
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, directed all District Election Officers on 2 November to re-examine every rejected Form 6 application so that eligible people are included in the roll, and said electors missing from the roll should be added by matching the rolls of panchayats with those of Assembly constituencies, Hindustan Times reported. He spoke at a meeting in Meerut at which he and the Commission's Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, Manish Garg, reviewed preparations for the 2027 Assembly election in 18 districts of the Meerut, Saharanpur, Moradabad and Aligarh divisions. He repeated the direction to re-examine every Form 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since the revision ended on 10 April (up-24), asked officers to see that applicants enter their mobile number and full address correctly on Form 6, and asked that operators of public service centres be trained in the online Form 6 and prevent multiple entries. Garg asked officers to verify the electors on the lists of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors and to pay attention to enrolling young voters and women.
items.quote: Missing voters should be included in the voter list by matching the electoral rolls of panchayat and assembly constituencies, he said at a meeting in Meerut on Monday.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report gives no count of rejected Form 6 applications in the state and does not say how the panchayat rolls are to be matched.
items.note: Hindustan Times, by Rajesh Kumar Singh, published 3 November 2026, 7:55 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 4 November 2026. Monday was 2 November. The report spells the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner's name Manish Garg. The Commission's officers directory (eci.gov.in/officers-directory) gives Maneesh Garg, as process.json does, and the claim follows the Commission. The paper's account of arrangements for polling day (webcasting, surveillance teams, sensitive booths) is about the election and is not carried. The earlier direction on Forms 6, 7 and 8 is up-24.

items.headline: U.P. to match Assembly voter lists with Panchayat and Urban local body rolls to find missing voters
items.claim: The office of Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer said in a statement on 4 November that the roll of every Assembly constituency in the state is to be matched with the electoral rolls of the panchayats and urban local bodies to find eligible people missing from the roll in the special summary revision, The Hindu reported. Guidelines were sent to every District Election Officer. Electoral Registration Officers are to have Form 6 filled for each eligible person found who is on no Assembly constituency's roll anywhere in India. District Election Officers are also to use the records of fair price shops run by the Food and Civil Supplies Department, and people aged 18 or more who are registered at a fair price shop in the district and are not on the roll are to be added if found eligible. Electoral Literacy Clubs in schools and colleges are to be activated for young voters, and the NSS, the NCC, Nehru Yuva Kendra, Yuvak Mangal Dal and the Bharat Scouts and Guides are to be brought in.
items.quote: Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh has directed that voter lists of all Assembly constituencies of the State be matched with Panchayat and Urban Body electoral rolls in order to find eligible citizens missing from the rolls during the Special Summary Revision of Voter Lists 2027.
items.response: The directions are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say how the rolls are to be matched or how many electors the matching has found.
items.note: The Hindu, by Sreeparna Chakrabarty, published 5 November 2026, 1:53 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 5 November 2026. Wednesday was 4 November. The statement itself was not found, and no second report was found. The estimate of about one crore electors to be added, which the paper attributes to unnamed sources, is not carried. The direction to match the panchayat rolls was first given at the meeting in Meerut on 2 November (up-31). The special summary revision's final roll in Uttar Pradesh is due on 4 January 2027. Awaiting the second reading.

items.headline: Panchayat, Urban Local Body Electoral Rolls in UP Collectively Have 3.45 Crore More Voters Than in Assembly List: Report
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, told The Times of India that the rural panchayat rolls finalised on 10 June 2026 hold 12.58 crore electors and the urban local body rolls published on 2 April 2023 hold 4.33 crore, 16.91 crore in all, against 13.46 crore electors on the Assembly rolls on 7 October 2026, a difference of about 3.45 crore, The Wire reported from that paper's report. He put the rural electors on the Assembly rolls at about 10.20 crore, about 2.38 crore fewer than the panchayat rolls hold, and the urban electors at about 3.36 crore, about 97 lakh fewer than the urban local body rolls hold. He said the difference is there although the Assembly rolls have four qualifying dates a year and the panchayat rolls one. He told the paper that the special summary revision could add more than one crore electors to the roll. Fair price shop dealers are to help find eligible residents who are not on the roll, and ASHA workers, ANMs, anganwadi workers and members of women's self-help groups are to work on enrolling women. By the report's figures the Assembly rolls held 15.4 crore electors before the revision began in October 2025 and 13.39 crore after it.
items.quote: “There is a clear difference between the two lists. This is despite the fact that assembly electoral rolls have four qualifying dates, whereas panchayat rolls have only one,” Rinwa told the newspaper.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The Free Press Journal reports that the State Election Commission prepares the panchayat rolls and the Election Commission of India the Assembly rolls, and it puts the difference between the panchayat rolls and the rural electors on the Assembly rolls at nearly 2.4 crore. Neither report says how many of the people on the panchayat and local body rolls are eligible for an Assembly roll or are already on one elsewhere.
items.note: The Wire Staff, published 6 November 2026 at 10:49 am IST (post_date_gmt 05:19:30), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) with curl on 6 November 2026. The Wire gives the figures as Rinwa's to The Times of India. That report was not found on 6 November 2026 on the paper's Lucknow page, its topic pages for Rinwa and the voter list, or by search, so the figures are given as The Wire reports them. The Free Press Journal (UP State Bureau, datePublished 2026-11-05T23:59:42+05:30) was read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl. It gives the rural difference as nearly 2.4 crore and the summary revision's dates (from 12 November, qualifying date 1 January 2027, final roll on 4 January 2027), and none of the other figures. 12.58 and 4.33 crore make 16.91 crore, and 16.91 less 13.46 is 3.45. The rural and urban parts as reported, 10.20 and 3.36 crore, make 13.56 crore, 10 lakh more than the 13.46 crore total, and the report does not explain the difference. The panchayat rolls are of June 2026 and the urban local body rolls of April 2023, so the two are not of one date. The 13.39 crore after the revision agrees with the final roll of 10 April 2026 (13,39,84,792). The Wire's own statements on the Election Commissioners' dissent, young voters and a national count of names excluded are not carried. The directions to match the rolls are up-31 and up-32, and Aaj Tak's account of the women's enrolment drive is in up-32.

items.headline: 1.27 crore Hindu voters missing from UP rolls … have appealed to EC: Yogi Adityanath
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, said at the Aaj Tak Panchayat programme in Ayodhya on 8 November that about 1.27 crore Hindu voters whose names are on the electoral rolls of the state's panchayat elections are missing from the Election Commission's rolls after the revision, and that the number of Muslim voters in the state rose by 1.65% after it, The Indian Express reported. In his words as the paper gives them, 66 lakh such voters are on the panchayat rolls, 55 lakh are Hindu voters who receive the benefits of government welfare schemes and are missing from the rolls, and 4.5 lakh are aged 18 or 19 and are missing from the rolls. He said a memorandum had been given to the Commission asking why this happened, and he appealed for these names to be included. Asked in the interview where the figure came from, he said that the rolls from before and after the revision are with everyone, in Aaj Tak's video of the interview. ThePrint reports him saying that about 46 lakh dead electors were on the rolls before the revision, and India Today and Aaj Tak report him saying that the names of about 46 lakh dead electors should be removed and the names of eligible voters should also be included.
items.quote: I am speaking about those 1.27 crore Hindu voters who have their names in the electoral list of UP panchayat polls, but their names do not exist in the electoral rolls of the Election Commission of India.
items.response: The Samajwadi Party president, Akhilesh Yadav, asked reporters how the Chief Minister had figures of electors by religion when the Commission had released none, ThePrint reported. In a post on X on 9 November he asked that Aadhaar be linked with voting, that metal cards be issued in place of paper or plastic voter cards, and that fingerprints or iris scans be used to identify voters, and he said the BJP would then be unable to have bogus votes cast. The party's spokesperson, Udaiveer Singh, asked the Chief Minister to explain how he got the data and to demand action against the Chief Election Commissioner and the state's Chief Electoral Officer, The Indian Express reported. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said he would answer all questions on the revision on 17 November, after the draft roll of the special summary revision is published. No reply from the Commission was reported.
items.note: The Indian Express, by Lalmani Verma, published 9 November 2026, 6:44 pm IST (modified 10 November, 5:46 am IST), read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 10 November 2026. ThePrint, by Prashant Srivastava, published 9 November 2026, 7:52 pm IST (14:22 UTC), read in full from the page text with curl on 10 November 2026. The Wire (The Wire Staff, published 10 November 2026, 12:45 pm IST, read in full through The Wire's CMS API) reports from The Indian Express, embeds Akhilesh Yadav's post on X and adds no figure of the Chief Minister's. India Today (Devika Bhattacharya, published 9 November 2026, 3:02 pm IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl) and Aaj Tak's text of the interview (Sweta Singh, datelined Ayodhya, 8 November 2026, read in full through Firecrawl) were also read. Aaj Tak dates the interview 8 November, and India Today's report of 8 November on another part of the same session (published 12:01 pm IST) says he spoke on Sunday, which was 8 November. ThePrint says Saturday, 7 November, when the programme also held sessions, and the item follows the other two. ThePrint gives the rise in Muslim voters as 1.63 per cent, and The Indian Express, India Today and The Wire give 1.65%. No report says whether the figure is a change in the number of Muslim voters or in their share of the roll. The Indian Express and The Wire say the BJP gave the memorandum, and India Today says his government did. His own words in every report are 'we'. No report gives its date or its text, and no earlier item in this file records it. 66 lakh, 55 lakh and 4.5 lakh make 1.255 crore, 1.5 lakh short of 1.27 crore, and no report says whether the three groups overlap or what accounts for the rest. The figures are the Chief Minister's own and were checked against no roll. Aaj Tak gives his answer on the source in Hindi, and the claim gives it in English. Aaj Tak's question was where the figure came from, and India Today gives the same answer to a question on whether the deletions raised doubts about the revision. His words in ThePrint, India Today and Aaj Tak on whose names should be removed besides the dead are not carried, because they are not needed to report what he said about the 1.27 crore figure. The Chief Electoral Officer's direction to match the Assembly rolls with the panchayat and urban local body rolls is up-31 and up-32, and the difference between those rolls as he gave it to The Times of India is up-33. The rolls before and after the revision that The Indian Express and ThePrint give, ThePrint's account of the Chief Minister's remarks of December 2025 and of deletions by district, and The Wire's comparison with studies of other states are not carried. The Chief Electoral Officer's answer on 17 November is due on the day the summary revision's draft roll is now to be published. The Commission's revised programme for Uttar Pradesh, which the Chief Electoral Officer announced on 10 November, put the draft back from 12 November to 17 November, and process.json records it.

items.headline: UP has 1.21cr fewer women voters than men, CEO orders special enrolment drive
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, directed District Election Officers on 4 November to hold a special drive to find and enrol eligible women before the 2027 Assembly election, because the state's rolls hold 1.21 crore fewer women than men, The Times of India reported. By the Commission's data for 7 October 2026 as the paper gives it, the rolls held 13.47 crore electors, of whom 7.34 crore were men, 6.13 crore women and 4,082 third gender electors. The paper puts the gap among women at about 1.71 crore against a projected adult female population of 7.84 crore, and the gap among men at about 99 lakh against a projected adult male population of 8.33 crore. It puts the projected adult population at 16.17 crore, a gap of nearly 2.70 crore from the roll, and says the difference does not necessarily represent eligible people who are not registered. Against a projected 84.47 lakh people aged 18 or 19, 19.62 lakh were registered on 7 October. ASHA workers, auxiliary nurse midwives, anganwadi workers and women of self-help groups are to find eligible women who are not on the roll and help them apply on Form 6 in the special summary revision.
items.quote: According to Election Commission data as of Oct 7, 2026, UP had 13.47 crore registered voters, comprising 7.34 crore men, 6.13 crore women and 4,082 third-gender electors.
items.response: The direction is the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say where the projected adult population comes from or how many women the drive is expected to enrol.
items.note: The Times of India, by Arvind Chauhan, Lucknow, published 5 November 2026, 12:58 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 10 November 2026. Wednesday was 4 November. 7.34 and 6.13 crore make 13.47 crore, and their difference is 1.21 crore. 7.84 less 6.13 is 1.71, 8.33 less 7.34 is 0.99, and 7.84 and 8.33 make 16.17, which is 2.70 crore more than 13.47. The paper's 13.47 crore for 7 October is the Chief Electoral Officer's 13.46 crore in up-33, rounded another way. 6.13 crore of 13.47 crore is 45.5 per cent, and the site's share of women in the final roll of 10 April is 45.46 per cent. The other directions the paper reports (matching the rolls with the panchayat and urban local body rolls, fair price shops, electoral literacy clubs, the NSS, the NCC and the youth bodies) are in up-32, and the enrolment of women through ASHA workers and others is in up-33.

items.headline: Ghaziabad to use Census to spot deleted SIR voters, bring them back on roll
items.claim: The Ghaziabad district administration will use the Census 2027 enumeration to find residents aged 18 or more who are not on the electoral roll and put them in touch with booth level officers to enrol, The Times of India reported. The decision was taken on 9 November at a meeting chaired by the District Magistrate and District Election Officer, Ravindra Kumar Mandar, to review preparations for the Census and the special summary revision. The paper reports that 5.7 lakh names (20.2%) went off Ghaziabad's roll in the revision, and 3.16 lakh in the Sahibabad constituency, which it says is the highest of any constituency in the state. It gives the Census self-enumeration as running from 16 to 30 November and the house-to-house enumeration from 1 December to 4 January. The meeting also reviewed the polling stations, and by the list the Commission approved the district, with the part of the Dhaulana constituency that falls in it, will have 865 polling centres and 3,073 polling stations.
items.quote: A decision to link the Census exercise with identifying eligible voters for inclusion in the electoral rolls was taken at a meeting chaired by district magistrate Ravindra Kumar Mandar, who is also the district election officer, on Monday to review preparations for Census 2027 and the SSR exercise.
items.response: The decision is the District Election Officer's own. The report does not say how the names found in the Census are to reach the booth level officers.
items.note: The Times of India, by Neetika Jha, published 10 November 2026, 1:27 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 10 November 2026. Monday was 9 November. The 5.7 lakh and 3.16 lakh are the paper's figures, and it does not say which count they are. The site counts 8,18,139 names left off Ghaziabad's draft of 6 January, 28.83 per cent of the 28,37,991 on the roll before the revision, and has no district or constituency figures for the final roll of 10 April. 20.2 per cent of 28,37,991 is about 5.73 lakh, so the paper's figure reads as the fall in the roll from before the revision to the final roll. The paper dates the summary revision's draft roll 17 November and the end of claims 16 December, as process.json does, and gives the final roll as 1 January 2027, where process.json gives 4 January 2027. The paper's account of the opposition's allegations and of the coming Assembly election is not carried. The state's count of polling stations after the Commission's approval is up-37.

items.headline: UP sees 3,786 fewer polling stations after ECI approval
items.claim: The number of polling stations in Uttar Pradesh fell by 3,786, from 1,77,516 to 1,73,730, after the Election Commission approved the District Election Officers' proposals for all 403 Assembly constituencies in an exercise carried out on 4 November at the norm of 1,200 electors to a polling station, Hindustan Times reported. The summary revision's draft roll is to be published at the 1,73,730 polling stations. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said the allocation began on 16 October. He directed District Election Officers to place booth level officers at the approved polling stations and to tell every elector whose polling station has changed in writing through the booth level officer. He also directed that all members of a family be entered in the same section of the roll, and that an elector found at a different polling station from the rest of the family after the draft be corrected on Form 8. The list of approved polling stations is to be given to the representatives of recognised political parties.
items.quote: Uttar Pradesh has witnessed a reduction of 3,786 polling stations, from 1,77,516 to 1,73,730, after the Election Commission of India (ECI) approved proposals submitted by district election officers (DEOs) for the allocation of polling stations in 403 Assembly constituencies across all 75 districts.
items.response: The figures are the Chief Electoral Officer's own. The report does not say how many electors were moved to a different polling station.
items.note: Hindustan Times, HT Correspondent, published 5 November 2026, 7:33 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 10 November 2026. 1,77,516 less 1,73,730 is 3,786. The report puts the final roll after the revision at 13.39 crore, 13.24 per cent below the 15.44 crore of 27 October 2025, and the site's figures (15,44,30,092 and 13,39,84,792) give 13.24 per cent. Ghaziabad's 3,073 polling stations on the approved list are in up-36.

items.headline: यूपी: वोटर लिस्ट से 3.38 करोड़ नाम गायब, पंचायत-निकाय की लिस्ट से खुलासा; हिंदू नाम ज्यादा कटे
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls hold 12.58 crore electors against 10.20 crore rural electors on the Assembly rolls, 2.38 crore fewer, and the urban local body rolls hold 4.32 crore against 3.31 crore urban electors on the Assembly rolls, more than one crore fewer, Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. Together the panchayat and local body rolls hold 16.90 crore electors and the Assembly rolls 13.52 crore, and the paper reports the difference as 3.38 crore electors missing from the Assembly rolls. It reports that the Election Commission has ordered the three sets of rolls to be matched, and that the matching follows an inquiry ordered by the High Court in Makdoompur village in Rae Bareli. Makdoompur's panchayat roll held 1,987 electors, of whom 1,549 were on the Assembly roll. After the matter was taken to the High Court, 448 electors missing from the Assembly roll were examined on the Court's direction. By the paper's account the Commission found that 44 of them had been moved to a neighbouring polling station and 290 were ineligible, shifted or duplicate, and 114 were eligible electors living in the village who were on the panchayat roll and off the Assembly roll, and their names were added. The paper says Form 6 is now being filled to enrol such electors. By its figures the Assembly rolls hold 7.37 crore men and 6.15 crore women, 834 women to every 1,000 men, and 2.04 crore names of dead, shifted and absent electors were cut in the revision.
items.quote: रायबरेली के मकदूमपुर गांव में पंचायत की मतदाता सूची में कुल 1987 मतदाताओं के नाम थे और उसमें से 1549 वोटरों के नाम ही विधानसभा मतदाता सूची में थे।
items.response: The report does not name the case in the High Court or date its order, and it does not date the Commission's order to match the rolls or say how the matching is to be done. It gives no date for its count of the Assembly rolls. No reply from the Commission or the Chief Electoral Officer is reported. The Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, has said he will answer questions on the revision on 17 November (up-34).
items.note: Live Hindustan, by Ashish Trivedi, Lucknow, published 11 November 2026, 5:36 am IST (modified 11:21 am), read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 11 November 2026. The JSON-LD names Ajay Singh, an assistant editor, as author, and the text carries Ashish Trivedi's byline, which the item follows. The report gives no date for the Commission's order or the inquiry, and the item takes the date of publication. The High Court order on Makdoompur was not found, and searches in Hindi and English on 11 November found no other report of the inquiry, apart from a YouTube video that reads out the paper's text. The report does not name the court. The Allahabad High Court is Uttar Pradesh's only High Court, and the tags record it. The spelling Makdoompur follows the report's मकदूमपुर. 1,987 less 1,549 is 438, and the paper gives 448 electors examined, which is 44, 290 and 114 added together. The report does not explain the difference of ten. 12.58 less 10.20 is 2.38, 4.32 less 3.31 is 1.01, 12.58 and 4.32 make 16.90, and 16.90 less 13.52 is 3.38. The rural and urban electors on the Assembly rolls as reported, 10.20 and 3.31 crore, make 13.51 crore, one lakh short of the paper's 13.52 crore. Against up-33, which reports the Chief Electoral Officer's figures to The Times of India, the panchayat and rural figures are the same (12.58 and 10.20 crore), the urban local body rolls are 4.32 crore against 4.33 crore, the urban electors on the Assembly rolls 3.31 crore against 3.36 crore, and the Assembly rolls 13.52 crore against 13.46 crore on 7 October. So the 3.38 crore is 7 lakh below up-33's 3.45 crore because this report's Assembly total is 6 lakh larger and its local body total one lakh smaller. Its 7.37 crore men and 6.15 crore women are each above the 7.34 and 6.13 crore of 7 October in up-35, so its Assembly count reads as a later one, and the report does not date it. The paper gives 54.54% men and 45.46% women. 6.15 of 13.52 crore is 45.49 per cent, and 45.46 per cent is the share of women in the final roll of 10 April in data/uttarpradesh/summary.json. The 2.04 crore is the fall in the roll from 15,44,30,092 before the revision to 13,39,84,792 in the final roll of 10 April (2,04,45,300). The names left off the draft were 2,88,74,067, and the paper's word for the 2.04 crore is cut. The paper's comparison by religion is not carried. It sets the fall in electors in Lucknow (22%), Ghaziabad (20.22%), Kanpur Nagar (19.92%) and Meerut (18.7%) against Rampur (10%), Saharanpur (10.48%) and Muzaffarnagar (10.38%), which it calls Muslim-majority, and 55,997 new electors in Lucknow West against 1.44 lakh fewer in Lucknow North, which it calls Muslim-majority and Hindu-majority seats, and from these it says more names of Hindu electors were cut. The report does not say how it decided which places are Hindu-majority or Muslim-majority or which count its percentages measure, the Commission publishes no count of electors by religion, and the item stands on the panchayat and local body rolls and on Makdoompur without it. Ghaziabad's 20.22% agrees with the 20.2% fall in the roll in up-36. The district figures in summary.json are of names left off the draft (Lucknow 30.04, Ghaziabad 28.83, Kanpur Nagar 25.50 and Meerut 24.65 per 100 on the roll before), so they do not compare. The paper's 1.65% rise in Muslim voters, 1.27 crore names of Hindu voters and 55 lakh beneficiaries missing from the roll are the Chief Minister's figures in up-34. The Chief Electoral Officer's directions of 2 and 4 November to match the Assembly rolls with the panchayat and urban local body rolls are up-31 and up-32, and the report does not say whether the order it reports is one of them. Recorded with wrong entries on the rolls, as up-33 is.

items.headline: यूपी: पीलीभीत मतदाता सूची में गड़बड़ी का मामला, निलंबित दोनों एसडीएम की जांच करेंगी मुरादाबाद आयुक्त
items.claim: Uttar Pradesh's Appointment Department has named the Moradabad Divisional Commissioner, Sangeeta Singh, on the Election Commission's direction, as the officer to hold an administrative inquiry against Mayank Goswami and Hemant Kumar Chaudhary, who were Sub-Divisional Magistrates of Pilibhit at the time and were suspended on allegations of malpractice in the revision of the roll of the Pilibhit Sadar constituency, Amar Ujala reported on 12 November. She is to go to Pilibhit soon, take the records and an account of events from the officials concerned, and then examine the allegations. The department's letter on the inquiry has been sent to the Pilibhit and Moradabad administrations. The paper recalls that after complaints about the constituency's roll in October the District Election Officer, Alok Kumar, sent the Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, an inquiry report that found irregularities in the disposal of 13,779 offline forms received between 31 May and 28 August, of which 10,470 were accepted and 3,309 rejected. On that report and the Chief Electoral Officer's letter, the Commission decided on 31 October to suspend the two officers, said they could not be reinstated without its prior permission, and wrote to the Chief Secretary for action.
items.quote: भारत निर्वाचन आयोग के निर्देश पर नियुक्ति विभाग ने मुरादाबाद कमिश्नर संगीता सिंह को जांच अधिकारी नामित किया है।
items.response: The inquiry is the state government's, on the Commission's direction. The report does not date the Appointment Department's letter or set a time for the inquiry, and it carries no reply from the two officers.
items.note: Amar Ujala, by Mukesh Kumar, published 12 November 2026, 10:32 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 12 November 2026. The report does not date the letter, and the item takes the date of publication. The report gives the period of the 13,779 forms as 31 May to 28 August, where the Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 22 October in up-22 and up-28 gives 31 May to 29 August, and the claim follows the report. The paper calls them offline forms, and up-22 records them as Form 8 applications. The paper calls the two officers the SDMs of the time, and up-30 records them as the Electoral Registration Officers of the Pilibhit constituency and gives the second name as Hemant Chaudhary. The suspension of 31 October is up-30. The two officers, the District Election Officer and the Divisional Commissioner are officials and are named. It follows up-21, up-22 and up-27 to up-30.
